summary: A strong, realistic IELTS listening paper. Every part has the right setting and length, and almost every question has a genuine trap (a date that is taken, a number corrected, two options mentioned and rejected). No wrong answers were found; only paraphrase pairs were added.
strengths: Part 1 traps on nearly every gap: 5th/12th November, 40/45 guests, Willow/Cedar Room, boardroom/theatre style, cake/biscuits, post/email.
Part 2 matching box is well paraphrased (shortest of people / greatest number; extra kit / special clothing; two hours before / arrive earlier) with two unused distractors.
Part 3 (882 words) is a convincing academic discussion; every MCQ rejects both distractors with reasons, and the multi-select items require following what is kept and what is left out.
Part 4 lecture is well organised, notes follow the talk's order, and Q37 has a fair distractor (tins vs later vacuum packs).

issues.problem: Some Part 4 notes repeat the lecture exactly (36 'plantations replaced large areas of', 37 'ground coffee stayed fresh in sealed', 39 'contains more'), so these items test spelling more than understanding.
issues.change: Reword the stems in a future edit, e.g. 36 'large areas of ______ were cleared for plantations'.

issues.problem: Q13 option B 'collected from the volunteers' office' repeats the speaker's exact words.
issues.change: Suggest 'They are given out behind the gift shop'.
